title: Iowa, Usually Red, Is in Play This Midterm as Economic Woes Mount
partialText: The Trump administration’s policies could cost Republicans in a state that is being hit hard by expensive diesel prices and uncertainty over trade.

title: Why Many Voters Are Unhappy With the Economy
partialText: With the midterms approaching, the economy is a top concern for voters. Our chief economic correspondent, Ben Casselman, describes which aspects of the economy have voters so frustrated.

title: Chris Pappas Could Make History in New Hampshire’s Senate Race
partialText: Chris Pappas, the Democratic nominee, would make history if he won. On the campaign trail, he doesn’t dwell on it.

title: How a Legal Backlash Against Big Tech Is Forcing Big Changes
partialText: A series of lawsuits has created a new de facto regulatory regime as courts order companies like Meta and Google to change their business practices — and pay up.

title: Mortgage Rates Remain Above 7%, Pushing Home Prices Lower in Some Areas
partialText: The 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage dropped slightly to 7.32 percent as prospective home buyers continue to struggle with affordability. But home prices are starting to drop in some areas.

title: Employers Shift Rising Health Care Costs Onto Millions of Workers
partialText: New surveys show that increases in premiums and deductibles are forcing people to forgo treatments or doctor’s visits while budgets are strained by higher food and gas prices.

title: Putin Nears a Prize: Restoring Ties With the U.S. While Giving Up Nothing
partialText: Russia has sought to separate the war in Ukraine from potential business deals and diplomacy with the United States. Its efforts now appear to be working.

title: PHP Security Flaw Sets Off Global Rush to Patch, Leaving Websites Offline
partialText: Governments and businesses around the world scrambled to prevent hackers from exploiting a vulnerability in PHP, a popular programming language.

title: What Is PHP? Why Are Government and Business Websites Going Offline?
partialText: A critical security flaw in the programming language underpinning much of the web has prompted a global rush to patch vulnerable systems.

title: A Young Family in Niagara, N.Y., and a Backyard Full of Radioactive Waste
partialText: A young family thought they had escaped the toxic legacy of Love Canal with a dream house near a creek in the suburbs. Then the men in the hazmat suits showed up.

title: Nicole Brown Simpson’s Sister: ‘We Deserve Answers’ on Accomplice Question
partialText: Tanya Brown said she believed someone helped O.J. Simpson get rid of the murder weapon. One of Mr. Simpson’s former lawyers called for a special prosecutor.

title: He Told Us About an O.J. Accomplice. Then He Said He’d Lied. What Next?
partialText: A source said his brother had been with O.J. Simpson the night of the murders in 1994. But when we refused to pay, he retracted his story.

title: Ebola Outbreak in Africa Reaches Widest Expansion Ever
partialText: Health officials are urgently seeking answers about the origins of a case newly identified in Nigeria, the first in that West African nation.

title: A.I. and Its Dangers Are Embedded In the Midterm Elections
partialText: The midterms are the first elections in which artificial intelligence is integrated into every major social media platform. Efforts to blunt its harms are uneven.

title: Impeachment. It’s Not Just for Presidents.
partialText: Trump’s grotesque rerun of the Gilded Age demands a rebuke.

title: A Shifting Standard
partialText: We look at how Title IX keeps changing.

title: Elizabeth Holmes Quote Drama
partialText: In today’s Backstory, the new Holmes film takes issue with our profile, Nikole Hannah-Jones unpacks her viral essay and a professor shares why he thinks we apply “conservative” and “liberal” labels inconsistently.

title: The Brief, Messy Political Career of Paolo Zampolli, a Trump Ally
partialText: He had an unlikely rise, from modeling agent to presidential special envoy. After his firing, he was unrepentant: “I need to make money.”
